headline: Tabled Tuttle Road sidewalk and school safety talks until April 2027; approved Round Hill Road sidewalks and Mellon Street culvert contract amendment.
summary: Members tabled the Tuttle Road sidewalk discussion until April 2027 and approved sidewalks to fill a gap on Round Hill Road. They also approved snow plow rate increases, budget transfers, and contract amendments for culvert engineering, and approved a policy on work within state roads. Staff said multiple engineering positions are vacant, which affects the level of service.
decisions: Accepted the July draft minutes and placed them on file; Council Member Hahn abstained.
Tabled the Tuttle Road sidewalk discussion for six months, to be revisited at the April 2027 Public Works meeting.
Approved installing sidewalks to fill the gap on Round Hill Road.
Accepted the consent agenda items, including employee recognition, the directors report, division reports, and the PW project list, and placed them on file.
Approved a $15,000 contract amendment with Stantec Consulting Services Inc., raising the contract from $225,200 to $240,200.
Approved the proposed policy on public works responsibilities and authority for work within state roads and right of way.
Authorized the Mayor and Director of Public Works to establish a five- to seven-member Safe Streets for All Committee and supported NVCOG's community outreach program and public survey.

Recommended that the City Council approve a Resolution in Support of Vision Zero / Safe Streets and Roads for All, with a goal of zero roadway fatalities and serious injuries within 20 years after the Safety Action Plan.
Authorized the Mayor to sign the CTDOT notice waiving the public information meeting and public hearing for traffic sign replacement on CT Routes 69 and 72.
Approved increased snow plow vendor rates, a $2,500 minimum yearly payment, and bids for a dedicated snow plowing contractor for Bristol Central, Bristol Eastern, and West Bristol schools.
Approved a $32,500.00 transfer of funds for the assistant City Engineer vacant position from regular wages to part-time wages.
Approved a $13,500.00 transfer for cleanup associated with the July 4, 2026 storm.

Approved an amendment to contract 2P25-045 with MMC Engineers for $38,5000 in structural engineering services for the Mellon Street culvert replacement, raising the contract from $133,317.36 to $171,817.36.
Referred to the Board of Finance a request for a bid waiver to procure a security camera vendor for the parking garages.
Approved an amendment to contract 2P25-044 with KS Engineers for $30,500 in structural engineering services for the Andrew Street culvert replacement, raising the contract from $192,000 to $222,800.
Accepted the storm cleanup thank you note and placed it on file.
Accepted the press release on the CTDOT draft statewide freight plan and placed it on file.
Supported a bid waiver and sent it to the Board of Finance.

plain_text:
1 
 
City of Bristol 
Board of Public Works 
Approved  Meeting Minutes 
For September 17, 2026 
With Zoom Access 
 
 
Members Present:  Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu 
    Commissioner Michael Dumas 
    Commissioner David Hartley 
    Commissioner Frank Stawski 
    Council Member Steven Seymour 
    Council Member Erick Rosengren 
    Council Member Gregory Hahn 
 
Staff Present:   Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works 
 
1. Call to Order 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. 
 
2. Approval of Minutes 
 
a. July Draft Minutes 
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and Commissioner Dumas to accept as presented and place on file. 
Motion passed. 
 
Council Member Hahn abstained from the vote. 
 
3. Public Participation 
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to move up item 5A up on the 
agenda. 
 
5    Old Business 
 
a. Tuttle Road Sidewalks-South Side School Safety 
 
Marion Cockayne, 93 Tuttle Road, shared her concerns and ideas regarding the Tuttle Road sidewalk and provided 
the board with a packet containing photos of the area. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu, reported that she reviewed the files from the previous year as well as files for the current year. 
Based on the review, several interim plans were initiated to address and help alleviate the issues.   
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, addressed his support of sidewalks, but stated that it is a 
Board decision. If decided to install of a sidewalk on the whole road, it would then become a capital improvement 
project. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu asked the board if they would be willing to table the matter with the understanding that the 
police department and the board of education will work collaboratively on this and would allow time to work 
through details and revisit the matter in the spring.
2 
 
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Hartley and Commissioner Stawski to table the discussion for six months and 
revisit on the April 2027 Public Works meeting. Motion passed. 
 
Council Member Hahn asked if during the winter months can we up the police presence.  
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu stated that these are items the Board of Ed will be working on to alleviate the traffic issues. 
 
Council Member Rosengren and Commissioner Hartley agreed the need for sidewalks and to have connectivity and 
that it should be revisited in the spring. 
 
 Commissioner Stawski raised the point about it needing a root cause analysis and mentioned it is also a parental and 
communication issue. 
 
Jeff Hayden, 50 Melinda Lane, voiced his concerns and ideas regarding the sidewalk issues and offered solutions for 
the issue. He mentioned big school events where parking is a large issue. 
 
John Smith, 103 Tuttle Road, spoke about his concerns with the sidewalks and spoke about the drop off times and 
the early of arrival of cars that wait for the school to open for drop-off. 
 
Round Hill Road Sidewalk  
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, reviewed the email submitted to the board regarding the 
sidewalks for Round Hill Road. The outcome will be sent to the resident with the timeframe for the project.  
 
Roger Plourde, 75 Round Hill Road, stated he does not feel this is a big problem, very little pedestrian traffic. He is 
not in favor of putting a sidewalk in front of his house. He feels speed is more of an issue on this road.  
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E, Director of Public Works, mentioned that the adjacent property owner supported the 
sidewalks, provided we took down the two trees. This sidewalk fills in a gap in that area.  
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Council Member Hahn to support and approve the 
installation of sidewalks to fill the gap. Motion passed. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu stated that they have received lots of requests for sidewalks in this area. The speeding issue was 
discussed as well.  Red Light cameras were briefly discussed, including how their use may influence driver 
behavior.  
 
Councilmen Rosengren spoke about phones calls he has received as well as the speeding issues and the sidewalks in 
this area, noting that how the addition of sidewalks would improve the connectivity throughout the area. 
 
Melvin Sherman, 634 Burlington Avenue, thanked the board and Mayor for their work. He also mentioned the great 
work the public works crews does for the city. 
 
Marion Cockayne, 93 Tuttle Road, asked about forming a committee and analysis about Tuttle Road. 
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu, stated it will be the operations committee of the board of education and they are just putting 
this in place.  
 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu took leave at 7:15 p.m.
3 
 
1. Consent Agenda 
 
a. Employee Recognition 
b. Directors Report 
c. Division Reports 
d. PW Project List 
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Council Member Rosengren to accept as presented and 
place on file. Motion passed. 
 
6. New Business 
 
 a.   BPW Resiliency Grant 
  
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, gave a brief update on the Re silience study including flood 
mapping updates.  
 
Antonio DiCamillo, Civil Engineer, Stantec, provided an updated presentation of the resilience study.   
 
MOTION:  made by Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Commissioner Hartley to authorize the 
Department of Public Works to execute a contract amendment to Contract 2P25 -016, Consulting/Engineering 
Services for Climate Resiliency Flooding/Storm Drainage, with Stantec Consulting Services Inc., in the amount of 
$15,000, increasing the contract amount from $225,200 to $240,200. Motion passed. 
 
b. BPW Responsibility on State Roads 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, presented the proposed policy for establishing public works 
responsibilities and the authority for work within the state roads and right of way. 
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Council Member Seymour to approve the proposed 
policy. Motion passed. 
 
c. NVCOG Vision Zero Update 
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Council Member Rosengren to Authorize the Mayor 
and Director of Public Works to establish a five- to seven-member Safe Streets for All Committee consisting of 
representatives from DPW, Police, Community Services, the Board of Public Works, Senior Center staff, and other 
appropriate stakeholders; and further support NVCOG's proposed community outreach program and  
public survey. Motion passed. 
 
MOTION:  made by Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Seymour to Recommend that 
the City Council approve the attached Resolution in Support of Vision Zero / Safe Streets and Roads for All, 
establishing a goal of zero roadway fatalities and serious injuries within 20 years following completion of the Safety 
Action Plan. Motion passed. 
 
d. NB CT DOT Sign Project 
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to Authorize the Mayor to 
sign the CTDOT notice waiving the requirement for CTDOT to conduct a public information meeting and pu blic 
hearing for the proposed replacement of traffic control signs along portions of CT Routes 69 and 72 within the City 
of Bristol. Motion passed.
4 
 
e. Snow Plow Fees 
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to Authorize the Department 
of Public Works to increase plow vendor rates to $120/hr. GVW 8,000 to 9,999 lbs.; $190/hr. for GVW 10,000 to 
17,999; $200/hr. for GVW 18,000 to 23,999 lbs.; and $255/hr. for GVW greater than 24,000 lbs. and loaders. In 
addition, the minimum yearly payment shall be $2,500, and the Department of Public Works shall obtain bids for a 
dedicated snow plowing contractor for Bristol Central, Bristol Eastern, and West Bristol schools. Motion passed.  
 
f. BOF Transfer 
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Dumas and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to approve the $32,500.00 
transfer of funds for the assistant City Engineer vacant position from regular wages to part time wages. Motion 
passed. 
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to add a BOF request to the 
agenda. Motion passed. 
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Dumas and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to approve the $13,500.00 
transfer the cleanup associated with the July 4, 2026 storm. Motion passed. 
 
MOTION: made by Council Member Erick Rosengren and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to add the Melon 
and Andrew Street culvert to the agenda. Motion passed. 
 
MOTION:  made by Council Member Erick Rosengren and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to authorize the 
mayor to execute an amended amendment to the contract 2P25-045 with MMC Engineers in the amount of $38,5000 
to provide structural engineer services for the Mellon Street Culvert replacement increasing the contract amount 
from $133,317.36 to $171,817.36.  Motion passed. 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works spoke about the reason behind the amendment being due to 
staffing in the engineering area of Public Works. 
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and Commissioner Stawski to add the security camera discussion to the 
agenda. Motion passed. 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works reviewed the funding the installation of cameras at Hope 
Street parking garage and the one at city hall. 
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Dumas and seconded by Council Member Seymour to authorize the Department 
of Public Works to forward a request for a bid waiver to the Board of Finance to Procure the services of a Security 
camera vendor for our parking garages. Motion passed.  
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Council Member Seymour to add a contract 
amendment for KS Engineers to the agenda. Motion passed. 
 
MOTION: made by Commissioner Hartley and seconded by Commissioner Stawski to authorize the mayor to 
execute an amendment to contract 2P25-044 with KS Engineers in the amount of $30,500 to provide structural 
engineering services for the Andrew Street culvert replacement from $192,000 to $222,800. Motion passed.  
 
 
Commissioner Hartley spoke about the issues trying to get a city engineer. And that Public works is in a staffing 
crisis for professional staff.
5 
 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E., Director of Public Works, mentioned he addresses staffing is in his directors’ report and 
that we have multiple vacancies in engineering and it directly effects the level of service that can be provided.  
 
Council Member Hahn and Raymond Rogozinski had a brief conversation regarding if it is a salary issue or a 
recruitment issue.   
 
2. Any other matter to come before said meetings and Communications 
 
a. Storm Clean up Thank You Note 
 
MOTION:  made by Council Member Seymour and seconded by Commissioner Dumas to accept and place on file. 
Motion passed. 
 
b. Press Release: CTDOT Draft CT Statewide Freight Plan for Public Comment  
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Dumas and seconded by Council Member Rosengren to accept and place on 
file. Motion passed.  
 
MOTION:  made by Commissioner Dumas and seconded by Council Member Seymour to support a bid waiver and 
send to the board of finance. Motion passed.  
 
8. Adjournment 
 
MOTION:   made by Council Member Seymour and seconded by Commissioner Hartley to adjourn at 7:47 p.m.  
Motion passed.  
 
 
 
 
_____________________________ 
Raymond Rogozinski, P.E. 
Director of Public Works
